poster_title: LongRAG: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Long-context LLMs
authors: Ziyan Jiang, Xueguang Ma, Wenhu Chen; University of Waterloo
paper_info: 2023; Combining RAG with long-context LLMs for open-domain question answering

panels.headline: Traditional RAG frameworks struggle with short retrieval units, leading to semantic incompleteness and hard negatives.
content: Short retrieval units (100-word Wikipedia paragraphs) put heavy pressure on the retriever.
This can result in the loss of contextual information and increased likelihood of hard negatives.
Recent advances in long-context LLMs allow handling up to 128K tokens, suggesting a redesign of RAG.
LongRAG aims to balance the workload between retriever and reader, improving overall performance.
The framework leverages long retrieval units and long-context LLMs to enhance open-domain question answering.

panels.headline: Imbalanced 'heavy' retriever and 'light' reader design in traditional RAG leads to sub-optimal performance.
content: Traditional RAG design is imbalanced, with a 'heavy' retriever and a 'light' reader.
Short retrieval units lead to the loss of contextual information and increased likelihood of hard negatives.
Existing RAG models require hundreds of short units and additional re-rankers to achieve high performance.
This inefficiency limits the scalability and effectiveness of RAG in real-world applications.

panels.headline: LongRAG framework uses long retrieval units (4K tokens) by grouping related documents or using entire documents.
content: The long retriever identifies coarse relevant information and retrieves only a few top units (1 to 8) without re-ranking.
The long reader extracts answers from the concatenated retrieval units (≈ 30K tokens) using existing long-context LLMs in a zero-shot fashion.
This design significantly reduces the burden on the retriever and improves overall performance.
panels.figure_caption: Traditional RAG vs. LongRAG. LongRAG operates on long retrieval units (30x longer) to reduce the retriever's workload.

panels.headline: Achieved EM of 62.7% on NQ and 64.3% on HotpotQA, comparable to fully trained SOTA models.
content: Evaluated on Wikipedia-based datasets (NQ and HotpotQA) and non-Wikipedia-based datasets (Qasper and MultiFieldQA-en).
NQ and HotpotQA documents were grouped to form 4K-token units, reducing the corpus size from 22M to 600K and from 5M to 500K, respectively.
Qasper and MultiFieldQA-en documents were processed as single units due to their average length being more than 4K tokens.
Improved F1 score to 25.9% on Qasper and 57.5% on MultiFieldQA-en, surpassing previous results.
panels.figure_caption: Comparison of different settings of LongRAG, using 200 test cases from the test set to evaluate various retrieval unit selections.

panels.headline: LongRAG significantly alleviates the burden on the retriever component, improving retrieval performance.
content: LongRAG reduces the likelihood of hard negatives and improves retrieval performance by using longer retrieval units.
The framework demonstrates effectiveness on both Wikipedia-based and non-Wikipedia-based datasets.
The use of long-context LLMs in a zero-shot setting shows promise but may benefit from fine-tuning.
panels.figure_caption: Retrieval performance on HotpotQA. Long-context retrieval significantly reduces the retriever's workload.

panels.headline: LongRAG provides a more balanced and effective approach to RAG by leveraging long retrieval units and long-context LLMs.
content: The framework significantly reduces the burden on the retriever and improves overall performance in open-domain question answering.
Future RAG systems should consider the granularity of retrieval units to better exploit the capabilities of long-context LLMs.
The performance improvement may be dataset-specific and requires further testing on a wider range of datasets.
The zero-shot setting of LongRAG may not always be optimal and could benefit from fine-tuning.
LongRAG opens new possibilities for more efficient and effective RAG systems in various domains.
